title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: Ministry of Higher Education, Ministry of Youth and Sports (MoYS), and private sector improved their ability to deliver career guidance and placement services. As a result of enhanced employability and career guidance services and English language skills trainings supported by ILO Youth for Future and Higher Education for Life and Work (HELW) projects 469 young people (328 F,141 M; 271 refugees and migrants, 198 Egyptians) were able to gain decent employment, 368 STEM graduate beneficiaries were employed in 95 SMEs. MOYS increased capacity to deliver inclusive Job Search Club (JSC) activities by capacitating 35 JSC facilitators delivered 46 trainings for total of 856 beneficiaries in 2 governorates (Assuit and Sharkia) in 2023. MoYS has made JSC more inclusive and 1049 young people (800 F, 249 M; 678 refugees and migrants; 371 Egyptians) have developed their employability and job search skills. PROSPECT governorates total 2621 beneficiaries were capacitated (64% F, 59% refugees, 4% PWD). MoYS introduced a new inclusive employability programme applying a sport for development approach. 1761 beneficiaries were reached to date (57% F, 46% refugees. Ministry of Social Solidarity (MoSS), supported by ILO implemented 4 employment fairs, with 11668 job seekers and 71 employers.National partners like Federation of Egyptian industries (FEI), Egyptian Engineering Export Council (EEEC), Ministry of Labour, MoSS enhanced quality of their apprenticeship delivery. They trained more than 2000 job seekers on employability skills. They trained and placed 500 job seekers in the white goods sector, 380 in readymade garment, 256 in Dairy sector. OSH training complemented the apprenticeship programme. Total of 668 beneficiaries to date have been trained (34% F, 19% refugees).Apprenticeship Inclusiveness system was increased following an integrated approach. Total of 643 apprentices were supported (38% F, 36% refugees) in Cairo and Alexandria. The ILO has contributed to the upskilling and employability of young Egyptians, refugees, and migrants via extending career guidance services, apprenticeship opportunities and skills development programs through governmental and civil society partners. To ensure partners are equipped to roll out and extend JSCs, the ILO has capacitated 48 staff (18 MOYS, 30 CSOs; 29 females, 19 males) to extend career guidance services to young job seekers. Additionally, an MoU with the MoYS was signed integrating the JSC and the Sport for Development activities in their annual workplan. Moreover, the ILO has contributed through: • 3 Career Service Management (CSM) Platforms introduced in 3 Public Universities • 120 beneficiaries received core skills training (composed of interpersonal and intrapersonal skills components) • 140 beneficiaries received 2 levels of English courses composed of 120 learning hrs (focusing on business English) • 95 SMEs were capacitated over three days on "Understanding the benefits of employing graduates for impact" • Facilitation of 225 internships with FEI. A sector round table including presenting sectoral recommendations for the white goods sector in the presence of the top management, the Egyptian Trade Union Federation (ETUF), the Engineering syndicate and workers was also organized in April 2023.

title.narrative: 5.3.2. Number of Member States with innovative, flexible and inclusive skills programmes and services targeting women, youth or persons in vulnerable situations
Output 5.4. Increased capacity of Member States to support digital transitions of skills development systems and develop digital skills

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Youth and Sports has revised its job search and employability skills training and digitalized it with the support of the ILO. The Maharati app which is free and accessible on the App stores has been rolled out accompanying the Job search club intervention. The app was further disseminated through NGOs and social partners throughout the year to support more youth to gain employability skills. 4,372 young refugees, migrants and Egyptians were able to access useful digital tools to further guide their skills development and job search efforts through the ILO developed and availed Maharati mobile application. The ILO’s Youth for Future (Y4F) project has developed the Maharati mobile application that seeks to provide a set of digital services to young people from identifying their skills, to preparing their CVs and cover letters, applying for job opportunities and preparing for a job interview. The Maharati app was further endorsed by the Ministry of Youth and Sports (MOYS) and shared with young job seekers through the ministry’s social media accounts and different events.
Additionally, the ILO, in collaboration with AWS, launched the re/Start Programme, targeting 120 refugees and HC, to build a diverse pool of entry-level Cloud talent. The programme also aims to match graduates with entry-level technical jobs. In collaboration with Microsoft and through the CARE Egypt Foundation, Digital Skills Development and Freelancing Programme was launched, aiming to support refugees and HC to become freelancers and acquire the necessary digital skills related to programming, as well as freelancing. 1962 refugees and Host Communities benefited from the digital skills development (53% F, 8% refugees), conducted jointly with Amazon Web Services (AWS).
In parallel, in collaboration with IBM and through the Education for Employment (EFE), the ILO is providing refugees and HCs with access to the IBM’s SkillsBuild portal, a learning path generating entry-level tech employment opportunities and providing free access to technical and professional training.
On a more systemic level the ILO is upgrading the JSC manual to include digital skills, such as basic digital skills required for online job searching, using online job portals and creating online applications, as well as the necessary digital skills that will help with job applications, such as developing a CV in Word, using email to communicate with employers, and so on. It is important to mention the new updated JSC version will serve not only PROSPECTS but other ILO projects.
